verdict: build, narrowly, and delete on the first upstream release that ships an agy binary
why: The thing this replaces does not exist. The operator supplied a note describing `agy -p "..."` as an installed Antigravity CLI. It is not installed: `command -v agy` is empty in WSL and in Windows PowerShell, and the only Antigravity executable on the machine is `Antigravity IDE/bin/antigravity-ide`, whose .cmd body invokes `resources/app/out/cli.js` and whose sh shim carries a Microsoft copyright and a VSCODE_PATH variable. That is a VS Code fork's editor CLI, the `code` equivalent; it opens files and takes no -p. The same note's MCP path is also absent: importlib.util.find_spec("google.antigravity.mcp_server") returns None on google-antigravity 0.1.9, so `claude mcp add antigravity -- python -m google.antigravity.mcp_server` would register a server that cannot start. So the build-vs-buy question is not whether to reimplement an existing CLI, it is whether to provide the one-file adapter that makes the operator's documented invocation form work against the one integration path that does exist, the Python SDK. 303 lines, of which the SDK call itself is about 20; the rest is a preflight that reports every missing piece at once, a data-boundary refusal, and a selftest.

alternatives.name: the vendor agy CLI
alternatives.covers: Does not exist as of google-antigravity 0.1.9. The PyPI wheel installs no `agy` console script; the venv's bin/ contains only dependency entry points (mcp, httpx, jsonschema, websockets). If a future release ships one, this component should be deleted rather than maintained, and that is the recheck condition.

alternatives.name: dot-claude/bin/a2a-gemini-call.py, already in this repo
alternatives.covers: Genuinely overlaps and was checked first. It calls generativelanguage.googleapis.com directly with urllib and returns a JSON blob. It is the right tool for a one-shot decorrelated review and it is what the agreement gate uses. It is not an Antigravity agent: no agent loop, no capabilities config, no streaming, no tool use, no session. Sharing its GEMINI_API_KEY convention rather than inventing a second one is the deliberate reuse here.

alternatives.name: tools/review/gemini_diff_review.py, also in this repo
alternatives.covers: Solves the data-boundary half well and the invocation half not at all. Its `looks_like_diff` refusal is the model this component's `--public` attestation and credential scan are copied from, and that reuse is the point. It is hard-wired to review a unified diff against a fixed schema, so it cannot carry an arbitrary prompt.

alternatives.name: the google-genai SDK directly, no wrapper
alternatives.covers: Different product. It is a model client, not the Antigravity agent runtime the operator asked for, and it would not give Agent/LocalAgentConfig/CapabilitiesConfig. Choosing it would answer a question nobody asked.

alternatives.name: an MCP server, so Claude Code calls Antigravity as native tools
alternatives.covers: This is the better shape and it is blocked, not rejected. The upstream module does not exist (see above), so building it would mean writing an MCP server around the SDK as well as this CLI. Worth revisiting at recheck: if the SDK ships mcp_server, the MCP path supersedes this file for in-session use and the CLI keeps only its shell/pipe role.

alternatives.name: no adapter at all, write the SDK snippet inline each time
alternatives.covers: This is the honest baseline and it loses on exactly one thing: the credential and classification gates. An inline snippet has no --public attestation and no secret scan, so every ad-hoc use is one paste away from sending employer or customer code to a free tier that the global contract forbids. The gates are the reason this is a file rather than a habit.

measured: Selftest passes with no credential and no network: 5 checks covering detection of a planted key shape, no false positive on prose, a refusal that names the kind of secret rather than echoing it, a missing-variable report, and a missing-venv report that includes the command that fixes it. Refusal order verified end to end: no attestation exits 4, a planted Google key under --public exits 5, clean attested text with no credential exits 3. One defect found and fixed during that run: with -p supplied and stdin an inherited pipe that nobody writes to, the first version blocked forever on read(); a terminal user never hits it and an automation user hits it every time.
open: Never executed against the live service. GEMINI_API_KEY is unset and no ADC file exists, so the SDK path is verified only as far as import and config construction. Vertex/ADC is supported by the SDK and is not wired here.
evidence: Read and run in full this session, not recalled. (1) `command -v agy` empty in WSL; `Get-Command agy` empty in Windows PowerShell; `find` over both Antigravity program directories returns only 'Antigravity IDE/bin/antigravity-ide' and its .cmd, whose body was read and is `"%~dp0..\Antigravity IDE.exe" ...\resources\app\out\cli.js %*` with a Microsoft copyright and VSCODE_PATH in the sh shim. (2) PyPI JSON for google-antigravity: 200, version 0.1.9, summary 'Google Antigravity SDK for building AI agents', requires_python >=3.10. Installed into a fresh venv with uv; `dir(google.antigravity)` lists Agent, AgentConfig, LocalAgentConfig, CapabilitiesConfig, GeminiAPIEndpoint, VertexEndpoint, ThinkingLevel and 20 more, matching the operator's snippet. (3) importlib.util.find_spec('google.antigravity.mcp_server') is None; the venv's bin/ was listed and its only console scripts belong to dependencies (mcp, httpx, jsonschema, websockets, distro, idna, normalizer). (4) Existing repo overlap read before writing anything: dot-claude/bin/a2a-gemini-call.py:1-38 in full, and tools/review/gemini_diff_review.py:88-137, which is where the GEMINI_API_KEY convention and the looks_like_diff refusal model came from. (5) Credential state checked by presence only, never printed: GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS and ANTIGRAVITY_API_KEY all unset; no ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json. (6) agy.py --selftest exits 0 with 5 named checks. Refusal order exercised end to end: exit 4 with no attestation, exit 5 on a planted AIza-shaped key under --public, exit 3 on clean attested text with no credential. (7) The gate's own security domain flagged agy.py:175 for a literal PEM header in the selftest and was right to; fixed by assembling the string at runtime rather than by adding it to gate.py PUBLIC_TEST_VECTORS, which would have blinded that scanner repo-wide.
recheck: Run all four; any one flipping re-opens the verdict. (1) Has upstream shipped the CLI this file substitutes for? `uv pip install --upgrade google-antigravity` then list the venv's bin/ for an `agy` entry point. If one appears, DELETE tools/antigravity rather than maintain it, and keep only the data-boundary wrapper if the vendor CLI has no equivalent gate. (2) Has the MCP path appeared? `python -c "import importlib.util as u; print(u.find_spec('google.antigravity.mcp_server'))"`. Non-None means the MCP shape supersedes this file for in-session use. (3) Is the direct-HTTP sibling still the better tool for one-shot review? Compare against dot-claude/bin/a2a-gemini-call.py; if this component grows a second caller doing plain one-shot prompts, the two should merge rather than diverge. (4) WebSearch "antigravity SDK CLI agy command line" and "google-antigravity mcp server" to catch a release note this repo missed.
what_ours_does: Provides `agy -p "..."` and `cat file | agy -p "..."` on PATH, the exact invocation forms the operator's note assumes, implemented over the google-antigravity SDK in an isolated venv. Reports every readiness blocker at once rather than one per round trip, refuses to send anything until the caller attests the payload is public and non-confidential, and refuses again if the payload carries a recognisable credential shape. Carries its own offline selftest.
strongest_counterargument: Nobody has run it against the live service, so the only thing proven about the SDK path is that it imports and that a config object constructs. Every gate in the file is exercised, and the one code path that matters, the agent call itself, is not. A reviewer would be right to call this staged rather than working, and the correct answer is that it stays staged until a GEMINI_API_KEY exists and the global contract's public-bundle condition is satisfied for whatever gets sent first.
